+"""A "(" after `name =` is read optimistically as arrow parameters. When the
+group turns out to be an expression, the functions inside it still count;
+likewise for `async`/`static` used as property names and for block
+statements, whose braces hold statements rather than object members."""
+
+import unittest
+
+from lizard import analyze_file
+
+
+def summary(filename, code):
+    return [(f.name, f.start_line, f.end_line, f.cyclomatic_complexity)

+        for filename in ("a.js", "a.ts", "a.tsx"):
+            with self.subTest(filename=filename):
+                self.assertEqual(expected, summary(filename, code))
+
+    def test_grouped_async_arrow(self):

+            "x = (async () => h());\n"
+            "const o = {\n"
+            "  b: (async () => { if (a) { return 1; } }),\n"
+            "};\n"
+            "function g() { return 1; }\n"
+        )

+
+    def test_async_parameter_name_still_a_parameter(self):
+        code = "const w = (async) => async + 1;\n"
+        self.check(code, [('w', 1, 1, 1)])
+

+        code = (

+            "  const d = (\n"
+            "    items.map((item) => {\n"

+            "    })\n"
+            "  );\n"
+            "  const e = (g((item) => item && 1));\n"
+            "  return d;\n"

metadata.body:
Fixes 7 parser cases where Lizard misses real functions (and their CCN) in JS/TS/JSX and Rust. We found them by running the current master and an older release over 11 open-source repos (caddy, eShopOnWeb, excalidraw, mastodon, monica, nest, redis, ripgrep, saleor, spring-petclinic, teammates) and checking every function the newer version no longer reports.

Each fix has a regression test that fails without it.

| # | Language | Example that lost functions | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Rust | `/*! ... src/**/foo.rs ... */` doc comment (ripgrep `globset/src/lib.rs`: 86 → 0 functions) | Rust block comments nest; the tokenizer ended the comment at the inner `*/` and parsed the rest as code | `rust.py` reads nested block comments whole, ignoring `/*` inside strings, raw strings and char literals |
| 2 | TS | `const r = f<S>(i, (b) => { ... })` | `>` before `(` was taken as a generic arrow `r = <S>(...) =>` | Only treat it as a generic arrow when the `<` follows `=` or `async` |
| 3 | JS/TS | `const a = { static: 1 };` / `x({ async: v })` | `static`/`async` was read as a member modifier and then swallowed the object's `}`; everything after was mis-nested (nest `core/injector/module.ts` lost 9 methods) | Followed by `:` `,` `}` `;` it is a property name |
| 4 | JSX/TSX | `<F>{(p) => (<I {...p}/>)}</F>`, `{open && (<b onClick={() => f()}/>)}` | The `{` of a JSX child expression was read as an object literal | Mark it as an expression brace |
| 5 | TSX | `<>#{this.title()}</>` | A lone `#` started a C-preprocessor macro token that swallowed the line | No macro tokens in the TSX template tokenizer |
| 6 | JS/TS | `x = (async () => h())`, `const d = (items.map((i) => {...}))` | The group was read as arrow parameters and then discarded | `async` after `(`, or a call/member access at the group's top level, means an expression |
| 7 | JS/TS | `function t() { { const r = find(xs, (v) => {...}); } }` | A bare block was read as an object literal | `{` at statement start is a block (guarded for `for ({a = 1} of b)`) |
| 8 | TS | `if (keys.includes(type as string)) {}` | `type` used as a variable started a type-alias skip that ran to the next `;` (nest `core/scanner.ts` lost every method after line 470) | A type alias name must be followed by `<` or `=`; otherwise the tokens are read as code |

Results on the 11 repos: 120,853 → 121,255 functions compared with master (e.g. mastodon `profile_edit.ts` 33 → 45, nest `module.ts` 47 → 70, nest `scanner.ts` 43 → 62). 9 files report fewer functions. In the 8 hand-written ones (10 entries in total), each dropped entry was a call inside a JSX ternary that master reported as a function, e.g. `{isSignedIn ? t("labels.signIn") : ...}` as a function `t`. The 9th is a minified bundle (`.yarn/releases/yarn-4.6.0.cjs`, 4250 → 4226), which both master and this branch already parse unreliably (master reports 41 functions there whose names are fragments of template strings).

Checks: the test suite has no new failures compared with master, `make pep8` is clean, and the pylint score is unchanged.
